description: A loading placeholder that mimics the shape of content while it is being loaded. It is a purely visual element with no semantic meaning. Skeletons should be hidden from assistive technology and paired with a live region that announces the loading state.

focus.notes: Skeleton is not focusable as it is a static placeholder element.

announcements: Skeleton itself should not be announced — it should have aria-hidden="true"
A surrounding container or live region should announce the loading state
screenReader.notes: Screen readers should be informed that content is loading via an aria-live="polite" region or role="status" container, not by the skeleton element itself.

contrast.ui: Skeleton uses a muted background with subtle pulse animation for visual distinction

consumerResponsibilities: Add aria-hidden="true" to skeleton elements to hide them from screen readers
Provide an aria-live="polite" region or element with role="status" to announce loading state
Include accessible loading text (e.g. "Loading...") for screen reader users
Once content has loaded, replace the skeleton and update the live region
